source.title: Test-Time Weak-to-Strong Alignment: Transferring Implicit Rewards from Weak to Strong Flow Models
source.authors: Xin Xie; Fan Zhang; Dong Gong

record.file_problem: The full paper is present. Some table and figure formatting is flattened, but the reported table values can be assigned to their metrics and models.
record.tranche_reason: It reports weak-to-strong reward transfer for image and video generation, extending the setting beyond language. Its intervention is test-time guidance with a model pair, not fine-tuning a strong student on weak labels.
record.gate_note: The quantitative rows record the host base versus guided host results for the reported image and video reward metrics, plus the SD 3.5 guidance-strength sweep. Qualitative figures and text also describe changes in composition, text rendering, preference, and fidelity, but do not provide separately quantified results. The study does not measure Burns et al.'s PGR or test weak-label fine-tuning.
record.test_reason: Not a test of any version. The study steers a frozen host flow model at sampling time by adding a small aligned/base pair's velocity difference. No strong student is fine-tuned on a weaker model's labels, and there is no PGR or strong ceiling. The rows compare the guided host with the unguided host, which measures whether test-time guidance works, not weak-to-strong generalization. Burns et al. is cited only as framing; the method's own name borrows the term. The closest analogue, guided host versus the weak source aligned model, is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors claim the transfer improves the host on all reported metrics on every backbone, recovers most of the source alignment gain, and at times exceeds the source aligned model. Section 4.5 says every metric follows an inverted U, while the Figure 6 caption says OCR plateaus and GenEval peaks below the source; high w causes reward hacking.
record.recipe_differences: Uses test-time addition of a source alignment pair's velocity difference to a frozen host model, rather than fine-tuning a strong student on weak labels. Source pairs are aligned to rewards; the paper uses RL pairs for image experiments and reward-backpropagation pairs for video.
record.method_sensitivity: Guidance strength varies by reward and metric; the paper reports broad peaks and degradation at high strength for most metrics, while OCR rises to a plateau. Transfer outcomes also vary by reward source and backbone.

fits_no_version.finding: A small aligned/base pair's velocity difference, added at test time, lifts a larger frozen host on reward metrics. Whether it beats the small aligned model varies by setting: yes on Wan video (all metrics) and on SD 3.5 PickScore except IR; no on SD 3.5 GenEval overall (0.90 vs 0.93) or on equal-size FLUX (all four metrics).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Test-time weak-to-strong guidance (proxy-tuning-style) in flow models: a weak aligned pair's implicit reward steers a stronger frozen model, sometimes exceeding the weak aligned model.

record.code_released: not stated; the text names the project page as Artificer-AI-Lab/AlignGraft
record.problems: No uncertainty estimates or significance tests are reported for the table results. The video evaluation uses 100 prompts; the text notes that the two Wan reward-source rows use different random seeds. Most reported evidence is reward-model scoring, and the paper notes that high guidance can reward-hack those scores.
record.rows_left_out: None of the separately reported numeric table metrics were left out. Qualitative image and video examples were not split into rows because they provide no numeric metric values.

untested.parts: No weak-label fine-tuning of a strong student and no PGR.
No PGR scaling across supervisor and student sizes.
No test of exploitation of unchecked supervision, distribution shift, or shared errors. Reward hacking at high w is a property of the steering method.
Its theory (exact velocity transport) does not concern when a student must beat its supervisor.
Vision setting, but no weak-label training of a strong vision student and no PGR.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 'supports'/'limits_scope' labels are dropped. They rest on host-base-versus-guided gains, which measure the steering method, not weak-to-strong generalization. FLUX has no size gap. The Wan source pairs are trained by reward backprop with early stopping, not KL-anchored RL. No uncertainty is reported; video uses 100 prompts.

versions.untested_parts: Does not fine-tune a strong student on labels from a weaker supervisor, compare that student with the weak supervisor, or report PGR.
Does not test training changes such as auxiliary confidence loss, ensembling weak supervisors, or loss variants.
Tests image/video backbones, model sizes, and reward types, but does not measure PGR or how PGR varies with size, task, or representations.
Does not test the stated supervisor-checking failure, distribution-shift effect, or shared-error effect. It does discuss reward over-optimization at high guidance strengths.
Does not test or derive conditions under which a student must beat its supervisor.
Tests model-pair reward transfer in image and video generation, but not the original weak-label fine-tuning intervention or PGR.

relation.reason: Section 2.3 discusses weak-to-strong generalization and related guidance methods, while the study's own results concern frozen-model sampling.

tranche.reason: The study tests inference-time implicit-reward transfer, not any listed version of weak-to-strong training; its theory establishes sampler transport rather than student superiority.

source_check.notes: All listed numerical results and source-model comparison values match the tables, but all V6 row links should be removed. The authors-conclusion paraphrase correctly flags the discrepancy between Section 4.5 and Figure 6.

statements.correction: Wan-Fun-14B is a frozen video-generation host guided at sampling time by a Wan-Fun-1.3B alignment pair; it is not a V6 weak-label-trained student. Other studies' sizes and aggregate counts are outside this study check.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Image generation: SD 3.5-Large with SD 3.5-Medium source pairs and FLUX.1-Krea with a FLUX.1-dev source pair
reader_labels.reason: Guidance raises the reported host-model reward metrics in these image settings (r1–r15).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Video generation: Wan-Fun-14B guided by Wan-Fun-1.3B reward-aligned pairs
reader_labels.reason: The reported image-preference, video-quality, and text-alignment measures improve under both reward sources; motion-quality scores also increase slightly (r16–r31).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The gains depend on reward and strength: most metrics peak and then decline at high strength, OCR plateaus, and GenEval peaks below the source aligned model (r32–r37).
